title: Mass-mass stoichiometry
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches mole ratios from a balanced equation to find one substance's mass from another's; the closest, Molar mass and moles, covers only mass-to-mole conversion and the balanced-equations card covers only balancing, so the mole-ratio step would be new material.

draft.title: Mass-mass stoichiometry
card: A balanced equation shows the mole ratio of the substances. In 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, 2 mol of H2 react with 1 mol of O2 to make 2 mol of H2O.
Equations give ratios of moles, not of masses. To use the ratio, first change the given mass to moles using n = m ÷ M.
Then use the coefficients in the equation to find the moles of the substance you want. Multiply the known moles by (wanted coefficient ÷ known coefficient).
Finally change moles to mass using m = n × M. The steps are: mass to moles, mole ratio, moles to mass.
draft.remember: Mass to moles, apply the mole ratio, then moles back to mass.

a.q: In 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, why can you not compare the masses of Mg and MgO directly using the coefficients?
opts: The coefficients give mole ratios, not mass ratios
The coefficients give mass ratios, not mole ratios
Mg and MgO have the same molar mass
Oxygen changes the mass of the magnesium
a.why: Coefficients in a balanced equation show the ratio of moles. Each substance has a different molar mass, so the masses are not in the same ratio. Treating coefficients as masses is the common mistake.
a.clue: What do the numbers in front of formulas count?

b.q: Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2. What mass of H2 (M = 2.0 g/mol) forms from 6.54 g of Zn (M = 65.4 g/mol) in excess acid?
b.why: n(Zn) = 6.54 ÷ 65.4 = 0.100 mol. The ratio of Zn to H2 is 1:1, so n(H2) = 0.100 mol. Mass = 0.100 × 2.0 = 0.20 g. Giving 0.10 g stops at the moles and forgets to convert to mass.
b.clue: Check the Zn to H2 ratio, then finish with m = n × M.

a.best: The coefficients give mole ratios, not mass ratios
